about.title: Academic training, research and the work behind the ideas.
about.intro: I am Mojtaba Roozegar, also written مجتبی روزگار in Persian. My academic and professional interests are rooted in agricultural economics, practical management and communicating research in ways that people can use.
paragraphs: My academic background includes a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Agricultural Economics from Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM), with a specialization in Production Economics and Farm Management. This field examines how agricultural enterprises allocate land, water, labor, capital and other inputs while considering costs, productivity and uncertainty.

I have described my scientific work as researcher and author, including the development of specialized books, educational materials and encyclopedic projects. These are areas of work and research interest; a specific publication or credential should only be described as completed when its details are individually documented.

My professional experience extends beyond agriculture. I have worked with gold, jewelry and coins, specialist handwoven carpets, cooking and hospitality, business training, and professional website development. These disciplines inform my interest in service quality, product evaluation and responsible enterprise management.

As founder and CEO of Zomorod Melal Agro-Industry Company and founder of MojPlayWin, I bring agricultural business experience into a new direction centered on research, AI-assisted tools, digital learning, original games and publication. This describes the intended emphasis of the work, not a claim that every proposed product has already launched.

activities.title: What my academic background is used to explore.
activities.intro: Agricultural production economics offers practical methods for choosing among limited resources; farm management connects those calculations to real people, workflows and risks.
paragraphs: Production economics: analyzing input and output relationships, production costs, gross margins, productivity and the sensitivity of decisions to price and yield uncertainty. These concepts become useful when comparing alternatives using consistent assumptions and evidence.

Farm management: examining crop choices, allocation of land and irrigation water, seasonal cash flow, labor planning and the interpretation of operational records. Useful analysis should disclose assumptions rather than present a single forecast as certain.

Research and education: turning technical material into careful explanations, specialist books, practical lessons and applied decision-support concepts. My wider experience in trade, hospitality and web development contributes to this approach. Any tool or educational product should be evaluated on its own merits before being described as commercially ready.

posts.title: How production economics connects research to a farm decision.
posts.intro: A research note informed by my reported specialization in Production Economics and Farm Management, within Agricultural Economics at Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM).
paragraphs: An agricultural enterprise faces scarcity in several forms. Available land is limited, water may arrive unevenly during the season, inputs must be financed before harvest, and prices can change after production decisions have already been made. Production economics organizes these trade-offs using a clear definition of inputs, outputs and the decision to be evaluated.

The first step is to choose a suitable unit of analysis, such as one crop in a field, a production cycle or the entire farm. Record quantities and units for seed, fertilizer, labor, machinery, irrigation and expected output. Next, separate costs that change when the plan changes from shared or longer-term costs. A partial budget or gross-margin comparison is useful only when the reader understands what has been included and omitted.

The second step is to identify binding constraints. If water is scarce, an alternative with higher revenue per hectare may not be preferable to one with a stronger contribution per unit of water. If working capital is limited, timing of payments can be as important as annual profit. Land quality, crop rotation, local regulations and market access must also be considered before an economic ranking is turned into a recommendation.

Finally, assess uncertainty. Change expected yields and selling prices over plausible ranges, examine what happens during a drier season, and ask whether the preferred alternative remains acceptable. A result that changes with a small assumption should be communicated as fragile, not as an optimal universal answer. A good report makes the reasoning reproducible and identifies where better measurements are needed.

This is educational discussion rather than farm-specific advice or a new peer-reviewed study. My aim is to connect academic reasoning to accessible tools and practical decisions, while keeping evidence, professional judgment and unanswered questions distinct.
